newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end up on hectic foreign fund bids.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end up on hectic foreign fund bids.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange ended higher in brisk trade as foreign institutional investors (FIIs) returned to the market in what brokers said was the begining of a pre-budget rally.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 8.42 points or higher at 721.02.
"FIIs are coming back to the market and it seems that a pre-budget rally has begun with only a month left for the budget to be announced," said Ashok Kaushik of brokers Analysis Securities.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is scheduled to present by February end the federal budget for 1997/98 (April-March).
Traders said encouraging statements from Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and the finance minister had helped trigger buying.

Deve Gowda told the Confederation of Indian Industry's (CII) annual meeting in Calcutta that the recent rise in stock prices was a clear indication of the government's commitment to boost industry and economic reforms.
He said the government would soon announce measures to attract more private domestic and foreign investment.
Chidambaram was quoted as telling the CII meeting tht he would take a decision on the controversial Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) on corporations soon.
The tax was introduced last year to plug loopholes in the legal system which allowed companies to avoid corporate tax.
State Bank of India gained 6.25 rupees to 236.40.
